name: SecureBio (charityevals)
beneficiaries_note: Our build: a pandemic kills people everywhere and the future lost is everyone's, so the result is spread by world population.
summary: SecureBio (Cambridge, Massachusetts) works against catastrophic pandemics: the Nucleic Acid Observatory's metagenomic early warning from sewage and airplane waste, SecureDNA's free DNA synthesis screening (since run by a Swiss foundation) and evaluations of how far AI models help with dangerous biology, run for AI developers. This model of all its work in 2024 (its latest Form 990, $4.25M) comes to about {{result}} years of healthy life per $1,000, from {{low}} to {{high}} on its plausible range: each dollar is valued as a typical project's cut in the forecast risk (Rethink Priorities' cross-cause model; the Existential Risk Persuasion Tournament's experts for pandemics, the AI slider for AI), the AI evaluations as work against AI misuse and the rest as pandemic work, deaths valued like every death (a COVID-scale pandemic's at COVID's age mix) and the future lost counted only where you count lives that never start (0% by default). The biggest uncertainties are the years a cut counts, the discount rate and how much a typical dollar cuts the risk (Rethink calls its figures placeholders; the range runs ten times either way). Every branch is discounted for missing data: no outcome of the work on the risk is measured.

sections.title: Other outcomes, in this model's unit

source.quote: In 2024, The NAO team conducted real-world biosurveillance of metropolitan sewage and airplane wastewater samples from selected US airports.

rows.explainer: Pathogen-agnostic early warning: deep metagenomic sequencing of municipal sewage and airplane lavatory waste (with CDC's Traveler-based Genomic Surveillance programme and Ginkgo Biosecurity), so that a new pandemic is seen before it grows exponentially. The project began in 2021 in MIT's Sculpting Evolution group and finished moving to SecureBio in November 2024.

rows.explainer: Free software that screens DNA synthesis orders (from vendors and benchtop synthesisers) against a hazard database kept secret by cryptography, tested with major manufacturers in 2024. SecureDNA is now run by an independent Swiss foundation (SecureBio's website); in 2024 SecureBio paid for its development.

rows.explainer: SecureBio's AI work is the template's misuse work by name: evaluations of how far models uplift dangerous biology (the Virology Capabilities Test and task-based tests run for AI developers), unlearning of dual-use biology and robustness against dual-use prompts (990 Part III line 4c). rows.label: AI evaluations: how far a typical AI project's effect applies
rows.explainer: Above a typical project: the developers use SecureBio's evaluations before release (SecureBio says references to its evaluations appear in the public system cards of Claude 3.7 Sonnet, Claude 4, GPT-4.5, o3-mini, o4-mini and Gemini 2.5 Pro; Anthropic's Claude 4 assessment used its Virology Capabilities Test and two more of its benchmarks). 1.2, the family's ceiling; down to 0.5 if the evaluations mostly confirm what the developers would have found.

rows.label: Pandemic work: how far a typical biosecurity project's effect applies
rows.explainer: The Nucleic Acid Observatory is the leading open pilot of untargeted wastewater sequencing, with CDC's traveller surveillance as a partner, and SecureDNA's screening was tested with major manufacturers; but neither the early-warning system nor the screening was yet in routine use in 2024, and detection helps only if a response follows. 0.75, our judgment with no reference class, 0.3 to 1.1.

rows.label: Weight: healthy years from the pandemic work (before adjustments)
rows.formula: bio_deaths_averted * ((1 - bio_covid_scale_share) * value_per_death + bio_covid_scale_share * covid_value_per_death) * dalys_per_death_value + bio_future_dalys
rows.explainer: The branch's deaths averted in healthy years (its COVID-scale part at COVID-19's age mix), plus its future healthy years kept: its share of the value, used to weight the adjustments so each applies to its own branch's value.

rows.label: How far a typical project's effect applies here
rows.explainer: The AI evaluations' and the pandemic work's multipliers, weighted by each branch's healthy years before adjustments (w_ai, w_bio), so each applies to its own branch's value: a dollar of the pandemic work counts about 1.1 times a dollar of the evaluations before adjustments.

rows.label: Share of the work no one else would have done now
rows.explainer: The share of the work no one else would have done now: others build DNA synthesis screening (IBBIS's Common Mechanism, commercial screening tools), run dangerous-capability evaluations (the developers themselves, the US and UK AI security institutes, RAND, Deloitte with Signature Science) and wastewater sequencing (CDC's National Wastewater Surveillance System, Ginkgo Biosecurity), but untargeted early warning at this depth is done by few. Our judgment, 0.7 (0.4 to 0.9); that the work would have come years later is in years_of_impact.

rows.label: SecureBio's share of the paid resources behind its outputs
rows.explainer: Partners' own work on the outputs: CDC's Traveler-based Genomic Surveillance and Ginkgo Biosecurity collect airplane samples, and the University of Missouri's lab sequences influent. The gene synthesis companies that take up SecureDNA and the developers that act on the evaluations are adopters: their part is under the mobiliser's share, not in this one (docs/normalization.md 2.24). Our judgment, 0.9 (0.7 to 1).

rows.label: This charity's share of the resources behind the outcome
rows.explainer: SecureBio's own spending over its spending plus the donated services, times its share of the partners' work (Convention 2): about 0.72.

rows.label: This charity's share of the good done with money, work or budgets it brings in
rows.explainer: The site's one setting for resources another party commits only because of the organisation (docs/normalization.md 2.24): governments' budgets and enforcement, companies' compliance, the use others make of research. The charity is credited this share of the good done with them, net of their cost; the rest stays with those who paid or did the work. Fixed.

rows.label: Share of credit used
rows.explainer: The share among co-advocates times the mobiliser's share: the rest of the credit stays with those who carry out the result (docs/normalization.md 2.24).

rows.label: Leverage and funging
rows.explainer: Whether large funders (Coefficient Giving, which gave $4M of general support over three years in November 2024 and $3.43M for the Nucleic Acid Observatory in February 2025) would give less if small donors gave more is the room factor of @next_dollar.securebio (docs/normalization.md 2.10), so it isn't asked again here (one question per adjustment): 1, our judgment, as for every catastrophic-risk model; 0.85 to 1.05 for funging the room factor misses.

rows.label: Counted less where the outcome isn't measured for this charity
rows.explainer: Thin: no outcome of SecureBio's work on the risk is measured; the cut per dollar is a typical project's from Rethink Priorities' model and the chances are forecasts, so the shared missing-data step applies (docs/normalization.md 2.12).

rows.label: All adjustments combined
rows.explainer: The product of the adjustments above.

rows.label: Benefits not modelled, as a share of modelled value
rows.explainer: Good beyond the catastrophes counted: the Nucleic Acid Observatory publishes its sequencing data and methods, which others use to track ordinary respiratory and enteric viruses; screening and AI safeguards also stop misuse far below a catastrophe. No such outcome is measured. 5%, 0 to 20%, our judgment with no reference class.

rows.label: Harm: speeding up dangerous capabilities, as a share of modelled value
rows.explainer: Beyond a typical project's backfire (in the shared cut): the Virology Capabilities Test is a capability benchmark that developers report and could tune toward, and evaluations map what models can do. −2%, our judgment, from −8% to 0.

rows.label: Harm: information hazards and attention, as a share of modelled value
rows.explainer: Beyond a typical project's backfire (in the shared cut): its published AI findings (a preprint on open model weights and pandemic agents, the Test's result that models outscore expert virologists) tell would-be attackers where AI helps, though the questions are kept private; SecureDNA keeps its hazard database secret by design and the Observatory's data carries little hazard. −3%, from −10% to 0, our judgment (the Johns Hopkins Center for Health Security −2%).
